newsitem.title: NORWAY: Flood begins under Icelandic glacier - scientist.
newsitem.headline: Flood begins under Icelandic glacier - scientist.

text.p: A giant lake under Europe's largest glacier in southeastern Iceland began flooding on Tuesday in a delayed reaction to a volcanic eruption beneath the ice cap last month, a scientist said.
"The flood started in the Skeidara river about three hours ago," Magnus Tumi Gudmundsson, a geophysicist at the University of Iceland in Reykjavik, told Reuters by telephone.
"The water has started to seep out from many parts (of the glacier) and it's rising very fast," Gundmundsson said.

Iceland has been bracing for massive flooding of the unpopulated black sand plains at the foot of the Vatnajokul glacier since the volcanic eruption melted large of parts of the ice cap and filled the sub-glacial lake Grimsvotn to overflowing.
No details of the scope of the flooding were immediately available.
Scientists had previously estimated the water from the brimming lake could surge out in torrents, flooding the surrounding plain, which is an uninhabitated sheep-grazing area.
